text:
pagerbot: INCIDENT ALERT — High 5xx rate detected on /v1/infer (us-west-2)
pagerbot: service=model-runner-prod, error_type=5xx, window=2m, count=320, threshold=50
pagerbot: pager routed to oncall group: infra-oncall

anya: taking pager — joining now :wave:

ryan: i'm on call. assigning myself. handoff: anya (infra), devon (runtime), maria (gateway)

devon: quick check — logs from model-runner show repeated OOM and segfaults. grabbing kernel oops and dmesg now.

devon: ```
[2026-03-17T09:42:10Z] infer-worker[pid=4218]: Alloc failed: GPU memory exhausted, requested=512MB
[2026-03-17T09:42:12Z] infer-worker[pid=4218]: segfault at 0 ip 00007f4a1b2c3d4 sp 00007ffd6a2b8230
[2026-03-17T09:42:12Z] kernel: [ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
```

maria: gateway metrics show increased latency and 502s from backends. Traffic spike started ~09:40 UTC and aligns with a canary rollout to quantized-2 model revision.

anya: can we confirm whether the backend fallback worked? runbook says to reroute to stable model variant if 5xx > 5% for 5m.

ryan: staging live route shows fallback didn't trigger — looks like runner instances are crashing before gateway can see healthy check failures.

devon: reproducing locally on a small test: quantized-2 with batch_size=8 triggers sudden memory growth in kv cache during long prompts. suspect regression in kv cache allocation on recent runtime commit 7f2a3c.

maria: mitigation proposal: 1) disable canary rollout (stop sending new traffic to quantized-2), 2) reroute traffic to stable-1 variant, 3) scale up stable pool by +20% while we triage.

anya: ack. I'll push a traffic policy to force stable-1 immediately.

anya: `curl -XPOST "https://console.redwood/api/v1/traffic" -d '{"route":"/v1/infer","variant":"stable-1"}'` -> accepted :white_check_mark:

pagerbot: change applied by anya at 09:45:37Z — routing to stable-1 variant

maria: initiating gateway drain for quantized-2: `kubectl scale deployment quantized-2 --replicas=0 -n prod` (dry-run then scale)

devon: I've captured a core dump from one of the crashed workers. uploading to /tmp/core-4218 and starting gdb unwind.

devon: `gdb --batch -ex "thread apply all bt" -ex "quit" /opt/infer/bin/runner /tmp/core-4218 > /tmp/core-4218.bt`

devon: bt shows kv_cache::grow() -> allocator::alloc_gpu() failing then calling a path that uses stale pointer after realloc. probable use-after-free in recent patch.

sre-ella: noting customer impact — 09:40–09:46 UTC saw elevated 5xxs, estimated affected requests ~1.2k across 40 customers. Top impacted: partner-acme (spike in errors for their endpoints), internal dashboard alerts.

maria: after routing change, 5xx rate dropped from 7.3% to 0.7% within 90s. latency trending back to baseline.

ryan: good. mitigation success. next: patch plan

devon: immediate hotfix: revert commit 7f2a3c on runtime and roll forward a strict patch that disables kv_cache auto-grow for quantized models. I can build and push a hotfix image.

anya: can we avoid another full rollout? Suggest canary the hotfix on a small subset (10%) and monitor for new OOMs.

maria: agree. will update gateway to send 10% to hotfix tag once image available. also keeping a manual rollback button ready.

devon: building hotfix image now — `docker build -t registry.redwood/runtime:hotfix-kv-20260317 .`

devon: pushed image, creating canary deployment `runtime-hotfix-canary` with 5 pods. starting canary at 09:57Z.

pagerbot: CANARY DEPLOYMENT STARTED — route update requested by maria, percent=10

maria: traffic split updated. monitoring dashboard... :eyes:

devon: initial canary pods stable, no OOMs in first 5 minutes, kernel logs clean.

anya: good. SLI check: 5xx for canary group = 0.3% over 6m. continuing canary for 20m then promote if green.

sre-ella: documenting customer comms: engineering to send a brief incident note to impacted customers and CS. draft will include window, root cause (regression in kv cache growth on quantized models), mitigation (traffic rollback + hotfix rollout), and ETA for full rollout.

ryan: editing post-incident checklist: open incident ticket, tag for postmortem, assign devon as owner for root cause analysis, anya for deployment fix and runbook update, maria for gateway automation test.

maria: I'll also add a new automated guardrail to abort canaries when backend 5xx > 1% for 3m.

anya: summary: immediate mitigation (traffic rollback) completed, canary hotfix in progress and stable so far. estimated full rollout after 30m of green canary. customer impact limited to 09:40–09:46 UTC, ~1.2k failed requests across 40 customers. no data loss reported.

ryan: thanks all. I'll keep this thread open for final confirmation post-rollout. please drop short status updates every 10m.

devon: noted — will post kernel log summary and full repro steps in the postmortem doc.

sre-ella: assigning severity P1 -> Retro required. tagging infra, runtime, gateway teams. preparing customer notification.

anya: closing handoff to oncall. ping if anything resurfaces. :thumbsup:

maria: 10m update: canary still clean, metrics look stable. preparing gradual promotion plan.

ryan: 30m update (09:45–10:15): promoting hotfix to 50% then 100% over next 15m. will confirm after 100%.

pagerbot: ROUTE CHANGE — promoted hotfix to 100% at 10:05:12Z

maria: done. all traffic on hotfix image. final checks ongoing.

devon: post-deploy checks clean. no further OOMs, no new segfaults. collecting artifacts for postmortem.

sre-ella: incident resolved. setting incident state=resolved at 10:12:05Z. please file postmortem within 72h.

ryan: resolving pager. great work everyone.
